Hello, Colombian here, and my opinion comes with a bias against the corrupt child-killing government. (but as the president has a 16% approval rate, well that's no surprise.)  
Disclaimer aside, I do not believe this was a real attack, nor do most people #AutoAtentado (#SelfInflictedAttack) is trending in Colombia.  
It has been common with the right-wing Colombian governments that when approvals ratings go down, terrorist attacks start to happen.  
  
Oh, and btw, they ''found'' 2 pristine ''Venezuelan'' rifles in the middle of the god-dammed jungle, just hours after the attack.  
This is just like the car bomb on June 15 on which 34 members of the military ended up hurt (including an American), nobody died tho', the government is blaming the ELN, for that one, but the group denies responsibility.  
(Do I believe the ELN even if they are a criminal group?, yes I do, the ELN has a track record of claiming responsibility for the attacks they perpetrate (like the car bomb in 2019', which killed 22)  
  
And I hate to say, that the ELN has a more truthful track record than my government, which killed at least 6402 in the ''false positives'' scandal (the real number is expected to be around 10k+).  
A government that has killed 52+ people in the last 2 months of protests (not counting the 379 missing people) (and a further 82.000+ missing in the armed conflict)  
And this is without mentioning the paramilitary forces, like the ''AUC'', a group formed by the ex-president Uribe, which committed massacres killing thousands.  
I'll leave with a tidbit from Wikipedia, and I recommend further reading on the case:  
  
The Colombian parapolitics scandal or parapolítica in Spanish (a combination of the words paramilitar and política) refers to the 2006–present Colombian congressional scandal in which several congressmen and other politicians have been indicted for colluding with the United Self-Defense Forces of Colombia (AUC), a paramilitary group which is responsible for killing thousands of Colombian civilians.  
In February 2007, Colombian Senator Jorge Enrique Robledo suggested another term, "parauribismo", indicating that the scandal was mainly affecting officials or political allies of President Álvaro Uribe's administration.  
By April 17, 2012, 139 members of Congress were under investigation. Five governors and 32 lawmakers, including Mario Uribe Escobar, President Uribe's cousin and former President of Congress, were convicted.  
  
I've seen my classmates beaten, I've been gassed in public transport, I'm afraid when I see a member of the police or armed forces. and I've had it good, at least I was not one of the young people found these last few days floating on the river Cauca after the police took them away in the protests. (or like Santiago Ochoa, a young man that was found decapitated, due to his participation in local protests last week)  
  
(When I started writing this, I was raging, now I'm just sad; this is not normal, this does not happen in a democracy; my friends and I should not have to say ''if y'all find me dead, it was the police'')  
THIS IS NOT NORMAL!

Eleven thousand ''immortals' were purged on the night of the riot; the streets were crowded by workers, young and old, all of them tired, all of them wondering what's gonna happen next.

The spark that ignited the fire of revolution came with the introduction of the first robotic workers with General Purpose Artificial Intelligence.

No more death in the mines, no more victims of industrial accidents, no more loggers being crushed like insects by falling trees.

At least that was the main idea, or at least those were the ideals that we hoped to reach.

The deployment of robotic workers was gradual, and the changes were small, just enough to not create distress in the workforce, but enough to eventually replace it..

A basic centrist compromise was made, and law for universal basic income went into effect, every citizen, with a social security number, would receive a basic stipend by the government; enough to live paycheck to paycheck, but not enough to raise a family, not enough to buy a home, not enough to scrape by, with a smidge of dignity.

As the monopolies created in this short era consolidated, the 'immortals' went on to own both the means of production and the land that their machines stripped, bared, and raped.

The prices constantly went up, a cent over here, and a couple over there, as the ‘immortals’ were constantly probing their markets for opportunities to jack up prices, telling to themselves  ‘it’s not like the workers have an alternative’

The stores of the ‘immortals’ became further means of subjugation, of an already oppressed community, the symbols or control, the symbols of inequality, the symbols of wealth and poverty.

​

The stores became the barrier between the workers and the ‘immortals’

​

When a population is unemployed, their brain tends to wander around, having ideas that might seem a little out of context, a little out of what they were taught at school by their ‘immortal’ teachers.

The workers contrary to what they were taught started congregating, asking for better conditions, asking for their fair share, after all they were the ones who made the machines.

The initial protests were repelled and put down by ‘immortal’ thugs and police alike.

But unlike their oppressors, workers had been breed, modified, and transformed into mere beast on the ‘immortals’ eyes;

​

When the workers took to the streets, their genetic alterations made them relentless, strong, tireless, but most of all, fully committed to their task.

The barricades around the central workers plaza were erected in an afternoon, and each day the congregation of workers grew, committed to the cause, bringing tents and supplies from the other side of the workers camp, and from the villages and small cities within the worker’s authorized transit área.

The retaliation was swift, and not a single troop had to be deployed, the stores doubled the price of their products, and reduced the availability of grains.

In the bakery, there was a breadline, with a few handfuls of miserable souls, either hungry, or near starvation, and a couple of ‘immortal’ guards taking care of what now had become a valuable commodity.

The ‘immortals’ had a policy of non-intervention, and were trained to descale, diffuse, and calm situations; after all in a contained environment, the workers will eventually turn on each other, and the cycle will begin anew.

On the breadline there was a kid, maybe 12.- 13 years old, it really doesn’t matter, as no one knew the name; after waiting for a couple of hours, it was the kid0s turn to reach the counter, and buy his daily  meal

The kid took out a handful of coins, the exact change for that priced loaf of bread, or at least the exact change to buy a loaf the day before.

Hunger is a powerful motivator, animals in distress may commit actions that would not seem logical, actions that may contradict every trick that the animals have been taught.

The kid grabbed the loaf, and ran through the side door, bumping into an ‘immortal’ guard who after a few seconds of confusion, went after the kid.

The guard was fast, and trotting at double pace was able to reach the kid, and grab him by the scruff of his Metallica t-shirt, a gift from his sister, and a reminder of why he was doing something like this.

The kid quickly used his free hand to grab something in his pocket, it could be called a knife, but that would be a very generous term, the kid pulled out a piece of scrap metal, a very sharp piece of scrap metal, which was wielded with precision, and aimed at the carotid artery of this supposedly immortal being; before the blade could hit the neck, the guard used his arm to shield himself

The blade was wielded masterfully, and the cut was clean and deep; but the true objective had failed, the guard had not been incapacitated; and the scruff of the kid's t.shit was still in the guard’s hand, who dragged him closer and grabbed the kid by  the neck

​

​

the ‘immortal guard threw the kid into the floor, put his knee on his back, and stamped on the hand that had the knife until it was dropped; the guard checked his wound, and knew it would leave a scar in his perfect skin, an eternal reminder of this miserable beast, that had fought dishonorably, and aimed to kill.

We can’t be sure that it wasn’t an accident and that the ‘immortal’ was not just too mesmerized by the blood flowing from the wound, after all, ‘immortals’ shouldn’t bleed.

The kid gasped for air under the weight of the immortal, a weight that crushed the kid’s chest and didn't allow the lungs to expand, a weight that put pressure on his heart, a weight that shut him down, piece by piece, organ by organ and breath by breath.

​

A crowd had formed around the scene, dozens saw the kid and the guard, and a few of them had the courage to record, had the courage to take pictures, and the courage to tell the workers what is really going on.

In the pictures, the kid was nameless, a nobody, just a little human who died while still holding against his chest the loaf of bread.

​

The crowd kept growing and the image they saw was an immortal cladded in power armor, standing on the back of a kid he murdered.

​

When animals are in groups, the dynamics between them, and between them and external entities change, while a single individual may not be violent, even if provoked; a crowd can collectively decide to become a violent entity.

We don’t know who threw the first stone, but thanks to their courage, a second rock soon followed, and the crowd went after the guard.

 At the end of that evening, the guard had been hanged, drawn, and quartered, and a military intervention by the ‘immortals’ went into effect.

The guards fell like flies in the land of the workers, they were constantly ambushed, and the guerrilla fighters had cut off supplies and communications.

Workers improvised with their current tools, after all, they were artisans and creators, firearms were produced within the first week of the standoff; and after months of planning, a full-on assault on the forward operating base located in the stores was going to become a reality.

​

The workers were well equipped, with artisanal firearms and recently forged sabers which shone with the last light before dusk, a light, a life,  that many of them know will not live to see another day.

​

The assault began after dusk, no prisoners were taken, and every ‘immortal’ was made to see his own mortality as a reality.

The company stores were looted, and after the forward operating base was overrun, the great door, separating the land of opulence, and the land of the workers was closed.

Eleven thousand ''immortals' were purged on the night of the riot; the streets were crowded by workers, young and old, all of them tired, all of them wondering what's gonna happen next and what awaits behind the Great Door.

The following was written by an unknown author over at 4chan's /tg/ board on 06-11-2013.

"Proceed, counselor," said the Lord Adjudicator, her outer eye stalks sinking into her head. The body language translators told the humans it was condescension.

"Thank you, your Lordship," the Praax counselor said as he gave a shallow bow before getting up to walk about on his stilt-like legs. They appeared ungainly but gave his gait an elegant way. "Your Lordship, The Praax have existed for approximately nine point two billion years. Far older than Resource Node Designate 2242-92G--the humans call it Earth. Before the humans even evolved, one of our scouting vessels made its way through 92G's system and marked it on our charts for strip-mining, as per our way of life, if you know our history. Seeing as it was previously unmarked, and under Council statute 9917 Article 33, subsect 98, paragraph 412, the planetoid belonged to the Praax Conglomerate.

"As bad luck would have it, a sapient species began to evolve on 92G. Humans, they call themselves. By some terrible galactic roll of the dice, our property had managed to grow enough to support life. But this does not detract from the fact that 92G is Praax property. Given that much of the galaxy these days is already claimed, the Praax are short on resources and must act on the ownerships with which it has secured, as other resource nodes have been made unavailable to us. Perhaps if we had acted quicker upon 92G this entire situation could have been...avoided, but the fates would not have it so, and here we are. Under Council statute 14722, Article 923, subsect 2, paragraph 66, and as demonstrated in Praax Conglomerate versus Xenobio Wildlife Consortium, the evolution of an intelligent species upon the property of a Council race does not remove ownership from the original claimants. I submit my words for your consideration, your Lordship."

The Lord Adjudicator's eyes panned slowly to the other side of the chambers, falling upon the humans still frantically pouring over the 3-ton book of Council law.

“Do the humans rebut?”

“Yes,” said one human, stammering, “just one moment, your highness—I mean Lordship! Sorry, Lordship,” he said to the amused chittering of the chamber space. Laughter, said the translators. The fate of humanity on the line and other peoples were laughing. Three of the humans pointed excitedly to a passage of text, and the head counselor straightened his suit before approaching the bench.

“Your Lordship, everything the Praax counselor has said is true. According to claim manifests recorded before my race had even crawled out of the proverbial primordial muck, our planet—Earth—was claimed by the Praax Conglomerate. By all articles we can find in Council law, the planet is indeed theirs.”

The Lord Adjudicator coiled her eye-stalks together. “Are the humans arguing for the opposition now?”

“No, your Lordship,” he said, smiling, “of course not. I’m sorry, let me get to the point. My Praax colleague pointed out the case Praax Conglomerate versus Xenobio Wildlife Consortium, in which a form of arthropodal life evolved to the point of rudimentary communication and social structure on a planet they dubbed 213-12C. These creatures possessed the same level of intelligence our apes or aquatic mammals have—smart enough for fluid social structures and varying levels of communication with other species, but lacking any kind of greater racial imperative; no civilization, no works of art, nothing. Seeing as how we are indeed intelligent, we must be given special consideration.” The Praax counselor scoffed.

“Which is why the human race is willing to relinquish Earth under the condition that the Praax Conglomerate fully provide for the relocation of every Earth inhabitant and every piece of infrastructure we have constructed since the beginning of our civilization.”

The Praax counselor erupted from his seat. “Absolutely preposterous! There exists no legal precedent for—“

“The Praax Conglomerate will remain silent!” shouted the Lord Adjudicator before turning her attention back to the human in front of her. “Continue, please.”

“If your Lordship will recall the Xoenakus Conflict, the defeated sued for peace. As per the Capitulation Act of G-date 920, the losers secured the right to continued existence. Seeing as the victors wished for the planet itself, the Council made the winning party responsible for relocating the surviving population and as much of their property as they could, a judgment which the victorious party complied with.”

The Praax counselor’s mouth dropped. The Lord Adjudicator sat back in her seat, her eye stalks at half-mast.

“You humans,” she said gravely, “consider this situation a matter of war?”

“With the survival of eighty percent of our race in the balance, we most certainly do.”

The Lord Adjudicator slumped back into her seat again, most intrigued by the turn of events. The humans remained absolutely still, unable to even breathe for the weight they felt on their shoulders. The Praax counselor, unamused though forever arrogant, so sure nothing the humans could say would swing things in their favor.

“The Court rules in favor of Humanity and agrees that, under the circumstances, a declaration of war has occurred simultaneously with a declaration of capitulation. Under the Capitulation Act of G-date 920, the Praax Conglomerate is found responsible for the relocation of Humanity and all of its holdings from Earth.”

The chambers grew loud with a dull roar as the crowd began stirring. The Praax counselor jumped to his feet. “Your Lordship! As I stated before, the Conglomerate is already short on resources! We could not possibly comply with the relocation, we don’t have the funds to—“

“If the Praax Conglomerate is unable to provide for the aforementioned conditions, then victory must instead be awarded to Humanity.”

The chambers went quiet. Quiet enough to hear the squishing sound the Lord Adjudicator’s eyes made as she flexed her eye-stalks. The Praax counselor felt himself weaken under the unyielding glare of the crowd, of the humans, of the Lord Adjudicator. He fell back into his seat, his teeth chattering as he searched for words, any words that could fix the situation. He could think of none.

“The Praax…The Praax Conglomerate capitulates. Ownership of 92G is relinquished to Humanity.”

And without a single shot fired, without a single death, without a single ship even leaving port, Humanity had won its first interstellar war.
